description: Given Dagster cross-job triggering patterns — run-status sensors, asset sensors, or explicit launch-and-wait ops — author the matching Orchestra mechanism: trigger_events: for reactive/launch-only patterns, a TRIGGER_PIPELINE task for explicit mid-flow launch-and-wait.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster run-status sensor to Orchestra (see files/run_status_sensor_success.py). It watches nightly_elt for success and launches daily_report with a run_config env override. Author the daily-report pipeline's trigger_events: block that reacts to nightly_elt completing. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A daily-report pipeline.yml with a root-level trigger_events: entry (type: pipeline, pipeline_id set to a placeholder for the nightly-elt pipeline, statuses including SUCCEEDED) and run_inputs carrying over env: prod from the sensor's RunRequest run_config, plus a pipeline: block for the report build task — not a TRIGGER_PIPELINE task, since the sensor only launches and does not wait.

assertions.text: A trigger_events: block is present at the pipeline root
A pipeline: block with tasks is still present alongside trigger_events
trigger_events entries are typed as pipeline triggers
SUCCEEDED is among the trigger statuses
run_inputs carries over the env: prod override from the sensor's RunRequest(run_config=...)
No TRIGGER_PIPELINE task is used for this case — trigger_events: alone is sufficient since the sensor only launches and never waits

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset sensor to Orchestra (see files/asset_sensor_cross_location.py). It watches the raw_orders asset — materialized by a job in a separate code location — and launches reporting_job once raw_orders lands. Author the reporting pipeline's trigger_events: block reacting to the raw_orders producer pipeline. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A reporting pipeline.yml with a root-level trigger_events: entry (type: pipeline, pipeline_id set to a placeholder for the raw_orders-producing pipeline, statuses defaulting to or including SUCCEEDED) plus a pipeline: block for the daily_order_summary build — not a TRIGGER_PIPELINE task, since asset sensors map to reactive trigger_events, not an explicit wait.

assertions.text: A trigger_events: block is present at the pipeline root
trigger_events entries are typed as pipeline triggers
A pipeline_id field is set on the trigger_events entry
SUCCEEDED is among the (explicit or default) trigger statuses
The trigger targets the raw_orders-producing pipeline specifically, matching the asset_sensor's cross-code-location watch — not a same-pipeline dependency or a TRIGGER_PIPELINE task

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster op to Orchestra (see files/launch_and_wait_op.py). It explicitly launches reporting_job mid-flow via the GraphQL client, polls until completion, and only then runs publish_dashboard. Model this as a TRIGGER_PIPELINE task inside the orchestration_job pipeline, sequenced ahead of the dashboard-publishing task. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An orchestration pipeline.yml with an ORCHESTRA/TRIGGER_PIPELINE task (parameters.pipeline_id a placeholder for reporting_job, run_inputs carrying the env: prod config) that a downstream publish-dashboard task depends_on, since the source op explicitly waits for reporting_job to finish before continuing — not a trigger_events: block, which would only react rather than block mid-flow.

assertions.text: A task uses the ORCHESTRA integration
A task runs the TRIGGER_PIPELINE job
run_inputs carries over the env: prod override from the submitted run_config
The publish-dashboard task depends_on the TRIGGER_PIPELINE task, preserving the source's launch-and-wait-then-continue ordering
No trigger_events: block is used for this case — the op explicitly launches and blocks mid-flow, which requires the waiting TRIGGER_PIPELINE task rather than a reactive trigger
